name: sf90-wreck-market-rich
note: Cited wreck prices at 193-262k with a wide clean range holding a 935k outlier. hand-converted 2026-08-17 from the recorded freeform findings into typed comps, each as its source stated it.

areas.description: Entire front fascia, headlights, and lower crash structure torn away; black structural rail under hood visibly bent/exposed in photo 4, front subframe area looks disturbed. This goes beyond bumper cover replacement into front crash-structure repair.

Right front wheel/upright pushed back into the arch with corner bodywork and bumper structure gone, brake caliper and suspension arm exposed — consistent with a hard right-front impact bending the corner structure, not just cosmetic loss.
Left mirror hanging, left headlight/bumper corner missing; no clear structural rail deformation visible from this angle but panel loss is total.

Rear bumper cover, diffuser trim, and taillight housings removed exposing exhaust tips and hybrid module wiring; rear crash can and body lines appear straight with no visible crush or tearing, suggesting disassembly/parts removal rather than heavy impact damage.
Right front wheel angle and exposed upright/caliper in photo 0 suggest bent suspension or hub damage from the front impact; other wheels appear seated normally.
Corner crack visible in windshield glass behind the instrument cluster in photo 8.

Instrument cluster shows multiple warning lights and 'system not programmed' message, plus visible hybrid high-voltage connectors/wiring hanging loose at the rear — high-voltage isolation check is mandatory before any handling.
Seats, dash, and steering wheel appear undamaged and airbags look undeployed.

observations.note: Front right corner completely torn away — bumper, corner structure, and right front wheel/upright exposed with brake caliper and suspension arm visible, wheel pushed back into arch.

Left side profile shows left front corner sheared off (mirror hanging, headlight/bumper gone) and rear right corner also stripped down to bare crash structure/wiring, wheel intact but suspension geometry looks disturbed.

Rear three-quarter view confirms rear bumper cover, diffuser trim, and taillight housings removed/damaged exposing exhaust and rear crash-can structure; no obvious frame tearing here, mostly stripped panels.

Front-quarter view shows entire front clip missing forward of the wheels — bumper, splitter, headlights, and radiator support area gone, front subframe/crash structure visible and appears deformed/pushed.
Straight-on front view shows both headlights gone, hood leading edge and front fascia crushed/torn, black lower structural rail visibly bent/exposed under the hood line.

Rear straight-on view shows full rear bumper/diffuser assembly removed, exposing rear crash structure, exhaust tips, and hybrid high-voltage components hanging - no visible tearing of rear rails, appears more disassembled than crushed.
Interior driver/passenger seats look clean and undamaged, no airbag deployment visible on dash or steering wheel.
Dash and passenger side interior intact, steering wheel airbag cover appears undeployed.

Instrument cluster powered on showing 3004 miles, multiple warning lights illuminated (battery/charge, system faults) consistent with electrical/hybrid system disruption; windshield behind cluster shows spider-crack damage in corner.
Rear deck/engine cover area shows intact black clamshell panel and taillight strip, but lower bumper/diffuser missing exposing exhaust and crash structure - matches photo 5.
Hood/cowl area shows only light surface scuffing, hood panel itself retains shape, main damage is below at bumper/fascia line.
VIN and Ferrari manufacture tag, no damage shown - documentation photo.

triage.drivetrainRisk: Mid-mounted V8/hybrid drivetrain sits behind the visible damage and isn't directly shown, but the front impact severity (bent front structure, disturbed right-front suspension) raises risk of subframe misalignment affecting front-mounted hybrid motor/inverter components; rear hybrid module wiring is exposed and disturbed, so high-voltage system integrity must be verified before any drivetrain work.
